newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: SABIC sees more Arab petrochem investmen.
newsitem.headline: SABIC sees more Arab petrochem investmen.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said on Monday it expected more future Arab investments in petrochemical industries.

"Saudi Arabia today is by far the largest Arab investor in petrochemicals, followed by Qatar and Bahrain," SABIC said in a paper presented to the third Arab petrochemical industry integration conference which opened in Bahrain on Monday.

"Many Arab countries will be increasing investments in petrochemicals. Announcements by Egypt, Kuwait, Oman, Abu Dhabi and Dubai have already been made about future investment plans for the rest of this century," SABIC said, but gave no details.
Many Gulf countries have moved into petrochemicals in a bid to diversify their oil-dependent economies.
SABIC, the biggest petrochemical producer in the Middle East which accounts for five percent of total world production of petrochemicals, is 70 percent owned by the Saudi government.
SABIC urged Arab investors to carefully study plans to set up new petrochemical plants and suggested establishing an Arab coordinating body to provide investors with information.
"Some degree of common planning and cooperation is required by the Arab world to make certain that new petrochemical plants are planned in step with global market requirements," he said.

"We should set up a petrochemical coordinating body in the Arab world that would provide its members with up-to-date statistics...not only covering petrochemicals but also general economic data," SABIC said.
